cards.note: Masculine. Nouns ending in -age are almost always masculine: le voyage, le fromage. Exceptions: la page, la plage, l'image.
Masculine despite the final -e. Nouns of Greek origin ending in -ème are masculine: le système, le thème.
Nouns ending in -ence and -ance are feminine. The indefinite article is used here because l'expérience hides the gender. Exception: le silence.
Nouns ending in -té are feminine: la liberté, la santé, la société. The exceptions are le côté and l'été.
An important exception: nouns ending in -eau are normally masculine, but l'eau is feminine. You say une eau minérale and l'eau est froide.

cards.de: The government has announced a reform.
cards.note: Nouns ending in -ment are masculine: le gouvernement, le bâtiment, le changement. This ending is a reliable gender clue.
Mouvement is masculine, because nouns ending in -ment are always masculine.

cards.fr: Le nature est magnifique en automne.
cards.answer: La nature est magnifique en automne.
cards.note: Nouns ending in -ure are feminine: la nature, la voiture, la culture. Le mur is not an exception, since it has no -ure.

cards.de: The situation has become difficult in recent months.
cards.fr: ___ situation est devenue difficile ces derniers mois.
cards.note: All nouns ending in -tion are feminine: la situation, la question, la solution. This rule has no exceptions.

accept: Cette décision a été une erreur.
cards.note: Like -tion, the ending -sion is feminine: la décision, la télévision, la discussion. So it is cette décision, not ce décision.

cards.de: I found a beautiful picture on the internet.
cards.fr: J'ai trouvé ___ belle image sur Internet.
cards.note: Image is one of the few exceptions to the rule that -age words are masculine. Also feminine: la page, la plage and la cage.

cards.de: On Saturday we are going to the beach.
cards.answer: Samedi, nous allons à la plage.
accept: Samedi, on va à la plage.
Samedi nous allons à la plage.
cards.note: Plage is feminine even though it ends in -age. That is why you say à la plage and not au plage.
Nouns ending in -eau are masculine: le château, le bureau, le gâteau. The article and the adjective must follow: ce château ancien. The one important exception is l'eau.

cards.de: The temperature dropped by five degrees last night.
cards.fr: ___ température a baissé de cinq degrés cette nuit.
cards.note: Nouns ending in -ure are feminine, including the many words in -ture: la température, la lecture, la peinture.
Feminine: la mer. The -er ending looks like a verb or a masculine noun, so English speakers often guess le.
Masculine: le lait. Nouns ending in -ait or -et are almost always masculine, and drinks like le vin, le the, le café follow the same pattern.
Feminine: la dent. Most nouns in -ent are masculine (le moment, l'argent), so this one has to be memorised.
Masculine: le pont. Short nouns in -on or -ont are usually masculine (le pont, le nom, le son).
Feminine: la chaise. Nouns ending in -aise or -ise are reliably feminine (la chaise, la valise, la surprise).
Feminine: la planète, as in sauver la planète. Careful, other nouns in -eme are masculine (le problème, le poème).
Masculine: le musée. Nouns in -ee are normally feminine (la journée, l'idée), but le musée and le lycée are exceptions.
Feminine: la main. Other nouns in -ain are masculine (le pain, le train), so la main must be learnt separately.
Masculine: le problème. The final -e makes English speakers reach for la, but Greek-based nouns in -eme and -ome are masculine (le système, le diplôme).
Feminine: la page. Most -age nouns are masculine (le village, le fromage), but la page, la plage and l'image are feminine.
Feminine: la colline, as in en haut de la colline. Nouns in -ine are almost always feminine (la cuisine, la machine).
Masculine: le groupe. A final -e does not mean feminine: le groupe, le verre and le silence are all masculine.
Masculine: le soleil. Il y a du soleil means the sun is shining. Nouns in -eil are masculine (le réveil, le conseil).
Feminine: la lune. Un clair de lune is moonlight. Remember the pair le soleil and la lune together.

cards.de: The butter is in the fridge.
cards.note: Le beurre is masculine, like le lait and le fromage. Many -eur words are feminine (la peur, la couleur), so this one is worth fixing in memory.
La clé is feminine, so the possessive is ma even if the speaker is male. French possessives agree with the object, never with the owner.
Un escalier is masculine and singular where English says stairs. Before a vowel ce becomes cet.

cards.de: My trip to Spain was wonderful.
cards.fr: Ma voyage en Espagne était merveilleuse.
cards.answer: Mon voyage en Espagne était merveilleux.
cards.note: Le voyage is masculine despite the final -e, so the possessive and the adjective both change. Adjectives must agree with the noun's gender.

cards.fr: Je ne partage pas ta avis.
cards.answer: Je ne partage pas ton avis.
cards.note: Un avis is masculine. Also, French never uses ta or ma before a vowel sound: it is mon avis, ton avis, son avis, even with feminine nouns.

cards.de: Today's newspaper is on the table.
cards.fr: ___ journal d'aujourd'hui est sur la table.
cards.note: Le journal is masculine, and the plural is irregular: les journaux. Nouns in -al usually form the plural in -aux.
Feminine. Careful: le page means a page boy, a young servant at court.
Le livre is a book. La livre is a pound, both the weight and the British currency.
Only the feminine means fashion: à la mode. Masculine le mode means way or method, as in le mode d'emploi (the instructions).

cards.de: Yesterday we visited the Eiffel Tower.
cards.note: La tour is a tower and is feminine. Le tour means a turn, a walk around or the order in a sequence.

cards.de: After the meal we always take a short walk around the neighbourhood.
cards.fr: Après le repas, nous faisons toujours ___ petit tour dans le quartier.
cards.note: Faire un tour means to take a stroll or go round the block. Here tour is masculine, unlike la tour (the tower).

cards.de: I'm popping over to the post office.
cards.note: La poste is the post office or the postal service. Le poste is a job, a post or a device such as a TV set.
